title: Nonfunctioning pituitary adenomas and sellar masses

steps.tx: Sellar neuroendocrine tumours are classified by dimensions into **microadenoma** when measuring less than 10 mm and **macroadenoma** when measuring 10 mm or larger. Every patient discovered with an incidental sellar mass requires comprehensive baseline hormonal evaluation, including screening for hypersecretion of **prolactin**, **IGF-1**, adrenocorticotropic hormone, and assessment of pituitary target organ axes to detect subclinical hypopituitarism.
steps.say: Pituitary tumours are categorized as microadenomas below 10 mm and macroadenomas at or above 10 mm in diameter. All sellar masses mandate complete biochemical screening for hormonal hypersecretion including prolactin, IGF-1, and 24-hour cortisol, alongside evaluation for secondary hypopituitarism.

vis.caption: Sellar MRI demonstrating pituitary lesion with suprasellar extension. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The majority of clinically nonfunctioning pituitary adenomas originate from the **gonadotroph** lineage, staining positively for transcription factor SF-1 and beta-subunits of FSH or LH. Because they do not secrete biologically active intact dimeric hormones, patients typically present late with mass effects, specifically progressive compression of the optic chiasm producing symmetrical or asymmetrical **bitemporal hemianopia** and hypopituitarism.
steps.say: Most nonfunctioning pituitary adenomas derive from gonadotroph cells and express steroidogenic factor 1. Because these tumours produce uncombined subunits without active endocrine syndromes, patients typically present with mass effects, notably compressive bitemporal hemianopia and hypopituitarism.

left.title: Gonadotroph Adenoma
points: Secretes free alpha or beta subunits

right.title: Somatotroph / Lactotroph
points: Secretes biologically active GH or prolactin

steps.tx: When evaluating an apparently nonfunctioning giant sellar mass with mildly elevated prolactin, clinicians must rigorously exclude a **macroprolactinoma** masquerading under the hook effect by repeating assays using **diluted prolactin** at 1:100. Erroneously misdiagnosing a prolactinoma as a nonfunctioning adenoma subjects the patient to unnecessary transsphenoidal craniotomy when complete pharmacological tumour involution could be achieved with oral dopamine agonists.
steps.say: Always exclude a macroprolactinoma by ordering diluted prolactin testing in patients with giant sellar lesions. The high-dose hook effect can mask massive hyperprolactinaemia, falsely suggesting a nonfunctioning tumour and leading to inappropriate surgical intervention when medical therapy is curative.

left.title: Hook Effect Masking
points: Sandwich assay produces falsely low optical density
Clinician assumes nonfunctioning adenoma with stalk effect
Risk of unnecessary transsphenoidal surgical resection

right.title: Serial Dilution Strategy
points: Guides definitive medical treatment with cabergoline

steps.tx: The benign suprasellar epithelial neoplasm **craniopharyngioma** exhibits a classic bimodal age distribution. The pediatric adamantinomatous subtype is characterized by somatic **CTNNB1** mutations encoding beta-catenin, displaying cystic machinery oil fluid and dense calcification on computed tomography. In contrast, the adult papillary subtype typically harbors activating **BRAF V600E** oncogenic mutations, presenting as solid suprasellar masses responsive to targeted BRAF-MEK inhibitors.
steps.say: Craniopharyngioma demonstrates two distinct molecular subtypes. The childhood adamantinomatous form harbors CTNNB1 mutations, showing cystic calcified lesions containing cholesterol-rich fluid. The adult papillary form is driven by BRAF V600E mutations, presenting as predominantly solid suprasellar masses.

left.title: Adamantinomatous Subtype
points: Driven by somatic CTNNB1 beta-catenin mutations
Cystic machinery oil contents and calcification

right.title: Papillary Subtype
points: Driven by oncogenic BRAF V600E mutations

steps.tx: A **Rathke cleft cyst** represents a non-neoplastic sellar and suprasellar cyst derived from remnants of the embryological stomodeal diverticulum. On magnetic resonance imaging, it typically presents as an intrasellar well-circumscribed non-enhancing lesion located between the anterior and posterior pituitary lobes. It frequently displays an intracystic non-enhancing proteinaceous nodule, which is hyperintense on T1-weighted sequences, distinguishing it from cystic adenomas.
steps.say: A Rathke cleft cyst is a benign embryological remnant located between the anterior and posterior pituitary lobes. On MRI, it appears as a well-circumscribed non-enhancing cystic lesion often containing a pathognomonic non-enhancing T1-hyperintense proteinaceous nodule.

steps.tx: Infiltrative inflammatory **hypophysitis** can arise from primary lymphocytic infiltration, systemic **IgG4**-related disease, or secondary to immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting CTLA-4. Contrast-enhanced MRI typically reveals symmetric infundibular **stalk** thickening, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot, and diffuse sellar enhancement. Unlike pituitary macroadenomas which erode the sellar floor, hypophysitis typically presents with disproportionately early anterior and posterior hypopituitarism.
steps.say: Hypophysitis can arise from autoimmune lymphocytic disease, systemic IgG4-related pathology, or immune checkpoint blockade. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates symmetric infundibular stalk thickening and diffuse homogeneous enhancement, with disproportionately early panhypopituitarism and central diabetes insipidus.

vis.caption: Sellar MRI showing infundibular thickening and sellar architecture. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Following endoscopic **transsphenoidal surgery** for sellar tumours, patients require intensive neuroendocrine monitoring for acute adrenal crisis, **cerebrospinal fluid leak**, and fluid-electrolyte disturbances. Postoperative diabetes insipidus may follow a classic **triphasic** pattern comprising immediate transient polyuria from axonal shock, followed by transient SIADH from degenerative vasopressin leakage on days 5 to 8, culminating in permanent diabetes insipidus if magnocellular neurons are destroyed.
steps.say: Postoperative care following transsphenoidal surgery requires close vigilance for adrenal insufficiency, cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhoea, and the triphasic fluid pattern. Transient diabetes insipidus gives way to hyponatraemic vasopressin release around day seven, followed occasionally by permanent diabetes insipidus.

steps.tx: True **pituitary carcinoma** is exceptionally rare and is strictly defined by the presence of non-contiguous craniospinal drop metastases or distant systemic metastases, rather than sellar histological atypia. For aggressive adenomas and carcinomas showing refractory progression despite maximum surgery and radiation, the oral alkylating chemotherapeutic agent **temozolomide** represents the evidence-based first-line systemic therapy, demonstrating biochemical and radiological responses in over 40% of cases.
steps.say: Pituitary carcinoma is strictly diagnosed by the demonstration of cerebrospinal or distant systemic metastases. In aggressive, treatment-refractory adenomas and carcinomas, oral temozolomide is the first-line systemic chemotherapeutic agent with documented objective responses.

left.title: Atypical / Aggressive Adenoma
points: Elevated Ki-67 index (>3%) and p53 expression
Confined to sellar and parasellar regions
Managed with surgery and stereotactic radiation

right.title: True Pituitary Carcinoma
points: Malignant transformation of lactotroph or ACTH cells
